passages.text:
Proposed Libyan Training Participants
[contact omitted] Sara Skahill
To:
[contact omitted] Khaled Koubaa
Thursday, October 6, 2022 at 9:33:22 AM Eastern Daylight Time
Dear Khaled,
I hope this message finds you safe and well! As discussed in Dubai, I am writing to put forward proposed partner
organizations to participate in Facebook training. Once you agree to the profile of organization, we will put forward
candidate names, organizations, and locations and can discuss timing of the online training session.
OTI's Libya team, the Libya Transition Initiative, is implemented by Chemonics, and they would like to put forward 20
candidates to participate in a Facebook training about media strategies and audience engagement.
For the pilot training, Chemonics would like to include 12 of its own Libyan employees so the team can better understand
how technical the training content is in order to better select future participants for another round, if applicable. The 12
participants are based in Tripoli, Benghazi, Sirte and Sabha.
The other eight proposed participants are representatives of OTI local implementing partners from across Libya, including
the following organizations and locations:
1 brgening melia anananton a anot ne uch e
organizing media campaigns that shed light on social issues, organizing social campaigns such as cleaning
campaigns, as well as cultural campaigns such as online educational competitions.
2. Zawiyat Al-Mahjub Scouts Regiment in Misrata, Libya. The Zawiyat Al-Mahjub Scouts Regiment is one of the
efforts.
3. Israr Organization for Development in Tripoli, Libya. Israr was established in 2016 as a non-profit organization
focused on issues of democracy and peaceful political transition in addition to issues of peace building and election
monitoring. The organization places within its work strategy the design and implementation of community studies
and research, training and empowerment of youth. The organization operates from its main office in the city of
Tripoli, and its team moves to various Libyan cities to carry out the projects which they oversee.
4. Albir is a Sabha-based local civil society organization. The organization focuses on peace building and positive
community engagement. In the past few years, Abir led successful advocacy campaigns to convey southern
communities demand to local and national governments.
5. Benghazi Scouts Regiment in Benghazi, Libya. The Benghazi Scout Movement is a voluntary, non-partisan
educational movement for young people. Its purpose is to contribute to the development of young people in
achieving their full physical, intellectual, emotional, social, and spiritual potential as individuals, responsible
citizens, and members of their local, national, and global communities.
6. Barah in Benghazi,Libya.Barah is newly formed non-profit organization whose main focus is art and culture.
Barah aims to create and nurture a supportive environment for civil society and artists.
7. Tanmia 360 (Libya Wide). Tanmia 360 is a Youth-led NGO aspiring to comprehensively develop the community
through conducting programs that enhance its community partnership.
8. Do Media (Libya Wide). Do Media is a media company that owns an audio channel (Radio Do FM), directed to all
segments of society, especially youth, through a variety of entertainment, awareness, cultural, social, technical,
respected fields and the local community. It provides media services in the field of creating visual content
presented on different social media platforms.

All of the candidates from this organization are aware that their names, email addresses and organizational affiliation will
be shared with Facebook for participation in the training. All of the candidates speak fluent English. If you are comfortable
with the profile and geographic spread of these candidates, I can send you their names and contact information and we
can schedule the pilot training. I'm happy to jump on a call tomorrow or early next week if it would be easier to discuss
next steps by phone!
Our Sudan team would like to put forward about 20 candidates to participate in a fact checking training, but are struggling
to find English speaking candidates. I hope to submit that list to you tomorrow. Like Libya, our Iraq team has expressed

interest in a media strategy and audience engagement training, but they are also struggling with finding English speaking
participants. I hope to submit that list to you tomorrow as well--apologies for the delay to our agreed timeline!
On that note, all three OTI teams (Libya, Sudan and Iraq) expressed interest in assembling a training of trainer in person
boot camp for bi-lingual English and Arabic speakers from the three countries who could then deliver trainings on the the
topics to wider audiences of our local partners. As we discussed, that could happen in the near year to allow plenty of time
for agenda development, planning and budgeting.
Best,
Sara
